title: Shopping for clothes: ¿me lo puedo probar?
summary: Name clothes and colours, ask for your size, try things on, say how they fit with quedar, and pay in the sales.
focus: Clothes shopping: sizes, probarse, quedar and paying
content:
## Twelve things to wear

| Spanish | English | Spanish | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| la camiseta | T-shirt | la chaqueta | jacket |
| la camisa | shirt | el jersey | jumper, sweater |
| los pantalones | trousers | el abrigo | coat |
| los vaqueros | jeans | los zapatos | shoes |
| el vestido | dress | las botas | boots |
| la falda | skirt | los calcetines | socks |

**Pantalones** and **vaqueros** are plural even for one pair: *unos pantalones negros*. Colours are adjectives and agree with the garment: *una camisa **blanca***, *unos zapatos **negros***, *una falda **azul***, *unos vaqueros **azules***. **Rosa** and **naranja** do not change: *una camiseta rosa*.

## Talla, número, probarse

Clothes come in a **talla** (pequeña, mediana, grande, or 38, 40, 42); shoes come in a **número** (un 42):

- *¿Qué talla tiene?* (What size are you? usted form.)
- *¿Qué número tienes?* (What shoe size are you? tú form.)
- *¿Tiene una talla más / menos?* (Do you have a size bigger / smaller?)

If the assistant asks *¿Te puedo ayudar?*, say *Estoy buscando un abrigo* or *Solo estoy mirando, gracias*.

To try something on, use **probarse**. It is reflexive, and the garment becomes a direct object pronoun placed after **me**:

- *¿Me lo puedo probar?* (Can I try it on? Said about el jersey.)
- *¿Me la puedo probar?* (Said about la falda.)
- *¿Me los puedo probar?* (Said about los zapatos.)

*¿Dónde están los probadores?* (Where are the fitting rooms?)

## ¿Cómo me queda? Quedar vs. quedarse

**Quedar** tells you how something fits or suits. It works like **gustar**: the garment is the subject and the person is **me / te / le**:

- *Esta camisa me queda bien / mal.* (This shirt fits me well / badly.)
- *El abrigo te queda grande / pequeño.* (The coat is too big / too small on you.)
- *Los pantalones le quedan estrechos.* (The trousers are too tight on him.)

The adjective agrees with the garment: *la falda me queda **corta***, *los zapatos me quedan **pequeños***.

**Quedarse** (reflexive) is a different verb. It means to stay and, in a shop, to take something:

- *Hoy me quedo en casa.* (Today I'm staying at home.)
- *Me la quedo.* (I'll take it. Said about la camisa.)

## Prices, sales and paying

- *¿Cuánto cuesta el vestido?* / *¿Cuánto cuestan los zapatos?* (How much is / are…?)
- *¿Cuánto es?* (How much is it altogether?)
- *Es muy caro. / Es barato.* (It's very expensive. / It's cheap.)

**Las rebajas** are the sales (January and July in Spain): *Está de rebajas, tiene un descuento del treinta por ciento.*

At the till (**la caja**): *¿Paga en efectivo o con tarjeta?* (Cash or card?) *¿Me da el tique?* (Can I have the receipt?)

To choose, use the demonstratives on their own as pronouns: *¿Cuál prefieres, este o ese? — Me llevo esta.* Since 2010 they are written without accents; older books still show *éste*, *ésa*.

quiz.explanation: 'La mediana' (medium) is a clothes size, and clothes sizes are 'tallas'. 'Número' is for shoes and 'precio' is the price.

quiz.prompt: For shoes you ask the size with a different word: ¿Qué ___ tienes? — El cuarenta y dos.
quiz.explanation: Shoe sizes are numbers, so Spanish asks '¿Qué número tienes?'; 'talla' is for clothes.
hints: Shoe sizes are given as a number.

quiz.prompt: You want to try on the dress (el vestido). You ask: '¿___ puedo probar?'
quiz.explanation: 'El vestido' is masculine, so the pronoun is 'lo', and the reflexive 'me' comes first: '¿Me lo puedo probar?'
hints: The reflexive pronoun goes before the object pronoun.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right form of quedar: Estos pantalones me ___ grandes.
quiz.explanation: Quedar works like gustar: 'los pantalones' is plural, so 'me quedan grandes'.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'I'll take it' (the shirt, la camisa)?
quiz.explanation: 'Quedarse' with an object means to take or keep: 'me la quedo' (la camisa). 'Me queda' is 'it fits me' and 'me quedo' is 'I'm staying'.
To ask the price: '¿Cuánto cuesta?' for one item, '¿Cuánto cuestan?' for several.
Cash is 'en efectivo', card is 'con tarjeta': '¿Paga en efectivo o con tarjeta?'

quiz.prompt: En enero hay ___ y el abrigo cuesta la mitad.
quiz.explanation: The sales are 'las rebajas'; in Spain they start in January and July.

quiz.prompt: ¿Cuál prefieres, la falda azul o la camiseta roja? — ___, la azul.
quiz.explanation: 'La falda' is feminine singular, so the pronoun is 'esa'. Demonstrative pronouns no longer need an accent.
hints: Which word is 'la azul' standing in for?

listening.meaning: This T-shirt looks very good on you, but the large size is better.
listening.note: Quedar works like gustar: the garment is the subject.

guide.tip: Three quedars: me queda bien (it suits me), me quedo en casa (I'm staying) and me lo quedo (I'll take it). Only the last two are reflexive.

bites.title: Size has two words
bites.rule: Clothes have a talla (S, M, L or 38, 40); shoes have a número (42). ¿Qué talla tiene? ¿Qué número tiene?

bites.title: Try it on: probarse
bites.rule: Probarse is reflexive, and the garment is a direct object pronoun after me: ¿me lo puedo probar? (el jersey), ¿me la puedo probar? (la falda).
bites.example_meaning: Can I try it on? (the skirt)

bites.title: Quedar works like gustar
bites.rule: Me queda bien / mal / grande / pequeño; plural me quedan. Quedarse is different: me quedo en casa (I stay), me lo quedo (I'll take it).
bites.example: Esta camisa me queda perfecta: me la quedo.
bites.example_meaning: This shirt fits me perfectly: I'll take it.

bites.title: Paying
bites.rule: ¿Cuánto cuesta? (one thing), ¿cuánto cuestan? (several). Pay en efectivo or con tarjeta. In the rebajas everything has a descuento.
bites.example: ¿Cuánto cuestan los zapatos? — Cuarenta euros, están de rebajas.
bites.example_meaning: How much are the shoes? — Forty euros, they're in the sales.

sorts.title: Talla or número?
sorts.why: Anything you wear on your feet has a número; everything else has a talla.

sorts.title: Queda or quedan?
sorts.why: The garment is the subject of quedar: a singular garment takes queda and a plural one, including pantalones and vaqueros, takes quedan.

sorts.title: Quedar or quedarse?
sorts.why: Quedar + bien/grande/pequeño describes fit; the reflexive quedarse means to stay or, with lo/la, to take something.

spots.sentence: ¿Qué número de camisa tienes? — La mediana.
spots.why: Clothes have a talla; número is only for shoes.
Pantalones is plural and is the subject: me quedan.

spots.sentence: Esta falda es bonita. ¿Me lo puedo probar?
spots.why: La falda is feminine, so the pronoun is la: ¿me la puedo probar?
Colours agree with the noun: la camisa blanca.
